title: Private Release Conductor and Migration Circuit for VPC/On‑Prem Rolling Upgrades
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Background: Customers running Redwood Private in VPC or on-prem environments require predictable, low-risk upgrade paths that preserve data integrity and availability. Current upgrade tooling is fragmented: ad-hoc scripts, manual DB migration steps, and cluster-level rolling actions that lack observability, transactional guarantees, and automatic fallbacks.

Goal: Build a 'Release Conductor' service plus a lightweight 'Migration Circuit' that together provide an orchestrated, auditable, and repeatable path for Private upgrades. The conductor coordinates ordered steps (preflight -> canary cohort -> schema migration -> full rollout) and the circuit enforces transactional boundaries, idempotency, and automated rollback triggers. This work should enable dry-runs, staged cohorts, and a single source of truth for upgrade state for each customer deployment.

Scope: Implementation covers: (1) a control-plane component (conductor) used by Redwood release infra and the Private control plane, (2) a migration circuit library that runs on the customer control plane to enforce step-level safety, (3) preflight checks and a dry-run mode, (4) telemetry and alerting hooks for SLOs, (5) operator/CLI for running and inspecting upgrades, and (6) documented runbooks for support/SE teams.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor API exposes create/run/pause/abort/status operations and records auditable step history
Migration circuit implements transactional step semantics: try/verify/commit/rollback and is idempotent for retries
Dry-run reproduces full step plan and reports potential breaking changes without mutating customer state
Canary cohort mechanism supports cohort size, duration, and automatic success/failure gating based on health checks and custom regressions
Operator/CLI can resume interrupted runs and reconcile state with control-plane logs
End-to-end test harness runs simulated upgrades against a staging cluster and a VPC-based mirror and produces a reproducible report
Telemetry exposes per-step latency, error rates, and user-visible SLO violations to Console dashboards
implementation_notes: Conductor will be a stateless control-plane component backed by an append-only upgrade log stored in the private control plane DB
Migration circuit is a small agent library (~Go) that exposes a CRD-compatible reconciler for k8s and a light adapter for non-k8s installs
Schema migrations must be expressed as explicit, reversible operations. For DBs we will prefer online-safe operations and introduce a staged apply pattern (shadow-copy -> backfill -> switch over)
All steps must declare a 'safety token' prerequisite (concurrency lock) to avoid concurrent upgrade attempts on the same customer
We will reuse existing rollout gating components where possible but implement a thin policy layer for private-specific constraints (maintenance windows, network egress limits)
Security: conductor -> customer control plane communication will be mutual-TLS and ops will require an audit trail for each action
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design): finalize API contract and CRD shape, spike 1: local operator + dry-run simulation
Phase 1 (Alpha): deploy conductor to internal infra, test with two staging VPC customers, iterate on rollback behavior
Phase 2 (Beta): enable cohort canaries for early adopter customers behind feature flag, expose CLI and console UI for rollouts
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default for all Private customers, provide one-click scheduled upgrades and documented runbooks
Safety gates: preflight checks, cohort health window, automated rollback on schema-validation or service-SLO breaches

2026-03-06 - Design review: Agreed to surface per-step preflight warnings in Console and require explicit human confirmation for non-reversible schema steps. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/infrastructure/private-release-conductor
